description: The design tokens Claw's own chrome draws with, so the notice banner on every client is the Control UI's card rather than a lookalike. This file is the ONE owner: desktop reads it as data (core/tokens.js) and iOS mirrors it as constants (mobile/Claw/NoticeTokens.swift), with a parity test asserting the mirror still equals this file.
why: The gateway serves the Control UI's stylesheet as a content-hashed asset under an immutable cache header, for example /assets/index-Cuu-imEh.js, and our chrome is a separate document, so that URL cannot be imported and must not be hardcoded.
What is genuinely shareable is the token layer. These are the values the Control UI resolves those tokens to, copied here with their source, so a drift is findable rather than invisible.

Nothing reads the gateway at runtime for this. A value here is a fallback that a live Control UI theme overrides where the names overlap (see desktop/src/chrome.js THEME_TOKENS), which is what keeps our chrome matching whichever palette the UI is actually running.

source.checkout: the OpenClaw checkout, not this repo
files: ui/src/styles/base.css (the :root block is the dark palette, :root:where([data-theme-mode="light"]) is the light one)
ui/src/styles/sidebar-issues.css (the attention card's shape, type and controls)
ui/src/styles/sidebar-attention-floating.css (the floating card's blur and hairline edge)

live.description: The tokens a client may take from a RUNNING Control UI, by name and kind, so both clients follow whichever palette the UI is actually wearing rather than only the default one. The desktop reads these from the gateway page and inserts them into our own pages (desktop/src/chrome.js THEME_TOKENS, injected by main.js applyThemeCss); the phone reads the same names from the same page and applies them to the settings and About surfaces. The names the UI does not publish (--danger, the card geometry) have no live value to take, so for those ui.css's own declarations stand.
whyItIsAnAllowlist: This list is not documentation: it is the filter. A gateway page reports whatever its theme has, and desktop/src/chrome.js sanitizeTokens keeps only the names here, so a palette token missing from this list cannot reach any of our pages however the Control UI defines it. The surface then keeps ui.css's copy of the Control UI's DEFAULT palette, and the page wears two palettes at once.

That is why --card and --bg-elevated are named here (2026-09-16) and why dropping one back out is a regression rather than a tidy-up. They were missing while ui.css's own comment already claimed a running Control UI overrides them, so on any palette that is not the default the settings GROUPS were painted from the default one: measured, the group read rgb(22, 25, 32) while the purple palette in force published rgb(31, 29, 46) for --card, inside a window that was itself the purple. The borrowed components are what made it visible: their surface IS this token, where ours was --panel, which the live theme can reach.

The guard is core/test/live-tokens.test.js: every colour ui.css declares as a palette fallback must be a name here or a stated exception, and the measured half is desktop/scripts/test-settings-theme.js, which opens our settings surface in the real app against a published palette and requires every declared colour to resolve to it. That harness is what fails when a name is dropped from this list: the page keeps ui.css's fallback for it, which is a two-palette page nobody can see in a diff.

ours.name: --focus-ring
ours.reason: ours: upstream publishes one, but this is the ring our own controls draw with

ours.name: --ok
ours.reason: ours: the Control UI has no --ok to take (see the tone note in the token spec)

ours.name: --warn
ours.reason: ours: the Control UI has no --warn to take (see the tone note in the token spec)

ours.name: --scrim
ours.reason: ours: the Control UI has no scrim to take, and this page writes its own

provenance.--bg-elevated: base.css :root --bg-elevated, the surface the attention card paints
provenance.--bg-hover: base.css :root --bg-hover, the card control's hover fill
provenance.--muted: base.css :root --muted, the subject line and the dismiss glyph
provenance.--accent-subtle: base.css :root --accent-subtle, reused for the info tone's tint
provenance.--ring: base.css :root --ring, the focus ring on the card's controls
provenance.--danger: base.css :root --danger, the colour sidebar-issues.css gives a critical row

shapeProvenance.--shadow-sm: base.css :root --shadow-sm, the attention card's resting shadow

typeProvenance.size.xs: base.css --control-ui-text-xs at the default --control-ui-text-scale of 1, the subject line
typeProvenance.weight.headline: sidebar-issues.css .sidebar-issues-panel__heading font-weight
typeProvenance.weight.subject: base.css body weight, 400

cardProvenance.radius: sidebar-issues.css .sidebar-issues-panel border-radius, the attention card's own
cardProvenance.surface: sidebar-attention-floating.css --sidebar-issues-background, the floating chrome's own mix, which is 92% of --panel; measured 2026-09-16, because this entry used to read --bg-elevated, which is the surface of the PANEL and a different colour in the light theme
cardProvenance.blur: sidebar-attention-floating.css backdrop-filter on the floating card
cardProvenance.padding: sidebar-issues.css .sidebar-issues-panel__summary padding, widened for a bar
cardProvenance.gap: sidebar-issues.css .sidebar-issues-panel__summary gap; measured 2026-09-16, because this entry used to read 12px against a rule that declares 8px
cardProvenance.edgeWidth: ours, the tone stripe the Control UI has no equivalent for
cardProvenance.dismiss.hoverSurface: OURS, and this one is a correction rather than a widening: it used to cite sidebar-issues.css .sidebar-issues-panel__dismiss:hover, which upstream does not declare at all (measured 2026-09-16). The interface's hover for the floating control lives on .sidebar-issues-button:hover, which fills with a 84% mix of --bg-hover and raises to --text, so the value here is taken from the interface's ordinary hover rather than from a rule that does not exist
cardProvenance.dismiss.hoverColour: OURS, for the same reason as the fill beside it: the cited rule does not exist, and --text-strong is our own choice of how far to raise the glyph

toneNote: One tone per notice, four tones, and all four are Control UI tokens rather than invented colours.

error takes --danger because that is the colour sidebar-issues.css gives a critical attention row, not --destructive: --destructive is the brand red this app already paints everything with, so an error edge in it would be invisible.
info takes --info rather than --accent for the same reason, and the Control UI has a real --info to take. It was --border-strong before this, which was quiet to the point of not being a tone at all.

The card in the reference screenshot is ONE tone of the Control UI's attention card in one palette. The structure is what we share here (surface, radius, type, the dismiss and the action), so all four of our tones are styled from the same card rather than the violet case being the only one that exists.
The glyph is for the clients that draw an icon. The desktop banner draws no icon and does not read it; that is the only part of this file one client ignores.
